releases.name: 0.2.0 — Local usage metrics
releases.body:
# 0.2.0 — Local usage metrics

The memory plugin can now show you what it has actually been doing — count-only, on your machine, never sent anywhere. This is the first feature release since 0.1.0 (0.1.1 was release-automation only): every commit in it is the local metrics work (ADR-0008, design spec §5.12), plus review-driven hardening. **No breaking changes** — the five-option config contract stands and no memory file, budget, injection, or hook-outcome behavior changed.

## Highlights

### `/memory-metrics` — the dashboard, on demand

Renders a deterministic markdown table and posts it into the session with **no model turn**:

- **Since / Explicit calls** — `memory_recall` / `memory_apply` tool calls, `/memory-review` invocations, and dashboard renders/resets (the read-only `memory_metrics` query is not counted — it changes nothing).
- **Behind the scenes** — hook activity (prompt, context, compaction, event-driven capture), budget-cascade outcomes (brief truncation, status sacrifice), capture results (captured / duplicate / retry / failed), and the hint → recall conversion: whether the tell-tale hint actually drives `memory_recall`, which was previously unknowable in production.
- **Memory health** — line counts of the six structural files vs their caps, handoff/archive/pending/seen counts (read-only, on request).
- **Budget pressure** — 7-day day-bucket view of where the 80-line injection budget went.

If the synthetic post is rejected, the command degrades to a single `memory_metrics` echo turn (§5.5 fallback) instead of failing. The `memory_metrics` tool returns the same table read-only.

### Privacy contract

- **Numbers only, everywhere.** No prompt text, tool output, captured paths, identities, or prose ever enters a metric — every persisted value is a JSON number, published counter names come from an enumerated fail-closed vocabulary, and the renderer is pure (tests assert the number-only invariant as a literal gate).
- **On-machine, bounded.** Counters live in the plugin-scoped `ctx.storage` under `<projectID>/metrics/…` (inside the OpenCode user data dir): monotonic totals, ≤90-day UTC day buckets (pruned lazily, no daemon needed), per-session hint arm entries that age out after one UTC day, and a lazy first-write `since` stamp. No network channel exists — dashboard and tool are the only surfaces.
- **No sixth option.** Metrics are always on; the control is `/memory-metrics reset`, which wipes the project's metrics keys under one lock and re-opens a fresh `since` window. Uninstall orphans the keys harmlessly, like the ledger.

## Hardening (review-driven, same release)

- Hint → recall arm consumption is **atomic** (`consumeArm`: read + clear in one locked body), so concurrent recalls convert an armed session at most once.
- Arm entries store an arming timestamp and expire after **one UTC day**; stale hints can no longer inflate `hint.recall`, and hinted-but-never-recalled sessions stop accumulating keys.
- Bumps are fire-and-forget and never throw; a 1,000-bump burst against a saturated storage queue cannot delay a hook (acceptance-tested).

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install opencode-nexusnv-memory@0.2.0
```

Nothing to migrate: existing installs pick up metrics automatically; there are no new config options or file formats.

## Compatibility

- Supported OpenCode range: `2.0.x`, built and type-checked against `@opencode/plugin 2.0.29` (pinned exact).
- Verify the install with `opencode plugin list` (shows `memory`).
- `/memory-metrics` deploy check (G-M1): the first resolved synthetic post logs one line — `[memory-metrics] synthetic posted (<session6>); confirm the table rendered without a model turn`. A rejected post logs nothing and falls back to the echo turn.

## Docs

- `docs/adr/0008-local-usage-metrics.md` — the decision, storage model, and residual-risk statement.
- `README.md` → "Metrics (local-only)" — what is counted, where keys live, reset/uninstall.
- Design spec §5.12 — the normative component contrac

First workflow-published release (validates npm trusted publishing).

- Release automation: OIDC trusted publishing replaces the default publish-token path; split gated build and minimal publish jobs with tag-on-main and tag/manifest guards.
- Staged only: CI stages the asserted tarball; approve on npmjs.com to publish.
- No plugin behavior changes since 0.1.0.

First npm release of the no-fuss memory plugin for OpenCode V2.

- Local-first project memory: six-file slice plus handoffs, budget-capped auto-inject, human-approved curation via /memory-review and memory_apply.
- Trust-boundary hardening from security review: column-0 section parsing, untrusted priors labelling, source-tag canonicalization, broadened secret redaction, project-scoped capture dedupe, location-less compaction drop.
- CI gates: typecheck, tests plus coverage thresholds on Node 20/22/24, gitleaks with canary-scoped allowlist, prod dependency audit, pack layout assertion.
- Published with provenance. Supported range: OpenCode 2.0.x.
